steps.description: Given a published release, when the author runs its MSI on a clean Windows 11 PC, x64 and then Arm64, then thermi, both services, the Start menu entry and the start at sign-in are installed with one UAC prompt and nothing downloaded, every executable and library under %ProgramFiles%\thermi is Valid for Get-AuthenticodeSignature, and uninstalling removes the folder whole and leaves %APPDATA%\thermi.

Given the previous release installed and used, with a saved style, "Start with Windows" off and a tray value shown in the taskbar, when the new MSI installs over it, then an update and a rollback run, then each time the settings, the style, the log, the start choice and the shown tray value are as they were.

Given a fake clock, when the service runs with updates built in, then it checks a minute after it starts, every 4 hours and after a resume past 4 hours, at the beta address only with the beta policy, never with Updates = 0 or in a build without a key, and on a metered network downloads only an urgent version.
Given a check, when the request the service sends is read, then it is one HTTPS GET of the channel's fixed address, with no query, no cookie, no identifier and the User-Agent `thermi`.

Given an update folder, when the manifest is too long, signed by no key or another, of another channel, an older sequence or expired, or the zip is longer, of another hash, holds an entry that leaves its folder or versions that are not the manifest's, or, in a release build, a file its catalog does not list, or the folder is a link or writable by users, then nothing under the folder changes, no version runs, and the event log names the check that failed; and a manifest signed by the backup key revokes the release key.

Given an installed version and a manifest, when the service plans, then it takes only a higher version that has not failed here and whose rollout reaches the PC's number, raising the rollout adds PCs and drops none, and a withdrawn installed version goes back to the kept previous one or stays without it.

Given a version ready, when a session has its window open, a drag under way or input within three minutes, then it is not quiet; when it has neither and is idle for three minutes, locked or has every overlay hidden, it is; and an urgent version waits only for the window and the drag.

Given an install folder with a process running from its launcher and a switch written down, when the switch is cut at each of its steps and the service starts again, then the launchers and the service's image path name the old version whole or the new one whole, the running process goes on, the next start runs the version the switch left, and only folders of versions neither kept nor running are deleted.

Given a switch in probation, when the new service serves no snapshot in 120 polls, or a second run of it ends without stopping within 10 minutes, then the PC goes back to the previous version and never takes the failed one again; a sleep of any length in between fails nothing, and an overlay that cannot switch gives up after 60 of its ticks.
Given settings a newer version wrote, with the earlier format's copy kept beside them, when the earlier version reads them, then it reads its copy and keeps the newer file beside it.
Given a recording, when the service writes its pipe's lines for it, then they are the golden file's, byte for byte.

Given channels with history, when the owner publishes, promotes, rolls back, disables and signs again, then each makes the next signed manifest, expiring 45 days later, a version below the channel's is refused, stable reaching past beta lifts beta, and rollback withdraws the version and offers the one before it.

Given each state of the updates, when About shows them, then it says up to date and when, a version ready, turned off by policy, the beta channel, no check for 14 days, or a build that does not update itself.
Given a check that finds a version, a download, a switch, a rollback and a refusal, when each happens, then the event log has one entry for it under thermi-sensors.

Given thermi installed for a test channel served from this PC, when a newer build is published, then it switches with no prompt while the author is away and the overlay never blinks; when the channel is rolled back, the PC goes back within a check; when a build made to fail at start is published, the PC goes back by itself and the event log says why; the service stays under 80 MB a day later; and once on R2, curl shows the manifest's max-age of 60 and the zip's immutable cache.

Given About asked for a check, when it reads the state, then it says it checks until the service has checked since a minute before the ask, for half a minute at most, then up to date, checked just now, or the version ready, which offers a restart only when its switch is not held.
Given the service, when About asks it for a check twice within a minute and once after, then it checks at once and then once more.
Given a version ready right after a quiet session's code, when About's restart asks for it while a check runs, then the switch begins once the check ends.

Given thermi installed for a test channel served from this PC, when About opens with a newer build published, then it says it checks, then that the version is ready with Restart to update, which switches and closes the window; reopened within a minute, it checks nothing more.

Given the service installed or not, a user's pipe owned by the user, SYSTEM, administrators or another user, a server process inside or outside the user's folder and at a lower integrity, and hosts that ended soon after their start, when the overlay picks a pipe and its next try, then it reads the service's whenever the service is installed, the user's only when all three checks pass, waits 2 s and then doubling to a minute after quick ends, and starts no host under the switch's lock.

Given the user's host started as the user, when an overlay connects and later leaves, then it serves the same lines on the pipe named for the user's SID, owned by that SID and closed to other users and remote clients, and ends with the Stopped mark once its last client left.

Given a per-user or a machine install, a channel offering the running version, a later one, an earlier one or none, a manifest that cannot be read, the policy Updates = 0, a download whose size or hash is wrong, and a prompt refused with 1223, when the fix is asked, then only a per-user install offers to install for everyone, msiexec starts only for the checked file the manifest names, held open and checked again through that hold, a manifest that cannot be read or a download refused changes nothing and says why, and a channel off, no MSI or the policy opens the download page.

Given a per-user install and a channel offering a newer version, when the user's host checks, then it takes it by the same rules, only from a folder no one but the user, SYSTEM and administrators writes, and switches through its own watchdog, run as the user; the watchdog's placing the launchers only once the new host serves is A28's, by hand, as A15 is for the service.

Given the user's host serving a client, when the watchdog sets its stop event, then it ends; and given an event of its name someone made first, then the host does not run, so no other process steers it.
Given a version published with its MSIs, when the manifest is read, then each processor's machine MSI has its URL, size and SHA-256, and a manifest without them still reads.

Given the user's installed products, per-user and machine, of thermi and others, when the machine's overlay looks for the per-user install to remove, then it finds only this user's own thermi by its per-user UpgradeCode, in the user's unmanaged context alone.

Given a standard user on a PC without thermi, when the per-user MSI installs, then no prompt shows and the overlay shows the GPU and the CPU's load with the CPU's temperature as "–"; when the person double-clicks it and an administrator consents once, to a prompt naming thermi that comes to the front even after a slow download, then the machine install, the service and the driver arrive, the CPU's temperature reads, the start at sign-in stays as it was, and the per-user install is gone with the settings kept. Run once more with the driver's download blocked: thermi installs, the event log says why, and the fix is still offered.

Given a per-user install for a test channel served from this PC, when a newer build is published, then it switches with no prompt and the overlay hands over; About's check and restart reach the user's host; the watchdog places the launchers only once the new host serves, and puts the old host back when a build that never serves is published; and the user's host measures within the service's budget, 80 MB and 3 % of a core.
Given the machine MSI's source, when its driver action is read, then ADDDRIVER is a secure property and the action runs only under NOT Installed AND ADDDRIVER = 1, so no repair adds the driver.
